(b) Minimum clear opening of the door shall be 0.90 metre and the door

(d) The water closet seat shall be 0.50 metre from the floor.

and/or lifts is required for the movement of differently-abled persons to areas 
of safety within a building. If possible, they could remain there until the fire is 
controlled and extinguished or until rescued by fire fighters. 


(a) A refuge area may be provided at the fire protected stair landing on 
each floor that can safely hold one or two wheelchairs. 


(b) The area shall have doorways with clear opening width of 900 
millimetres and 


(c) The area shall have an alarm switch installed between 900 millimetres

MATERIAL AND CONSTRUCTION METHODS. - (1) Quality of Materials and 
Workmanship: 


(a) All materials and workmanship shall be of good quality conforming 
generally to accepted standards of Public Works Department of 
Uttarakhand and any technical government department of Uttarakhand, 
Indian Standard Specifications and Code as included in Part V Building 
Materials and Part VII Constructional Practices and Safety of National 
Building Code of India as amended from time to time. 

(b) All burrow pits dug in the course of construction and repair of buildings, 
roads, embankment and the like shall be deep and connected with each 
other in the formation of a drain directed towards the lowest level and 
properly sloped for discharge into a river, stream, channel or drain and 
no person shall create any isolated burrow pit which is likely to cause 
accumulation of water which shall breed mosquitoes.

installation, air conditioning installation and installation of lifts and escalators shall be 
carried out in accordance with Part VIII Building Services, Section - 2 Electrical 
installations, Section - 3 Air- conditioning and Heating, Section - 5 Installation of Lifts 
and Escalators of the National Building Code of India as amended from time to time.

41. ENERGY CONSERVATION MEASURES. - (1) Use of Compact Fluorescent 
Lamps and Electronic Chokes: 


(a) The use of incandescent lamps and conventional chokes in all new 
buildings, institutions constructed in Government sector, Government 
Aided sector, Boards and Corporations and Autonomous bodies is 
banned. 


(b) It will be mandatory that in these existing buildings the defective 
incandescent lamps and chokes when replaced would be replaced by 
only compact fluorescent lamps (CFL), LED and electronic chokes. 


(c) The Competent Authority will effect necessary modification in the local 
demand to promote the use of Compact Fluorescent Lamps, LED and 
electronic chokes instead of conventional bulbs and chokes while 
releasing/sanctioning new connections/loads in such buildings. 


All new cases may consider the following provisions of solar water heating 
systems for energy conservation: 


(a) An open space in the roof which receives direct sunshine; the roof shall 
have a load bearing capacity of at least 50.0 kg per Square metre. 


(b) The building must have a provision for continuous water supply to the 
solar water heating system. 


(c) The building design should provide for an insulated pipeline from the 
heating system to all distribution points where hot water is required. 


(d) The recommended minimum capacity of installation shall not be less 
than 25 litres per day for each bathroom and kitchen subject to the 
maximum of 50 % of the total roof area is utilized by the system. 


(e) Installation of Solar Assisted Water Heating Systems shall conform to 
BIS specification IS 12933. The solar collectors used in the system 
shall have the BIS certification mark. 


Whenever hot water requirement is continuous, auxiliary arrangement either 
with electrical elements or oil-based systems of adequate capacity may be 
provided. 

No new building in the following categories shall be sanctioned unless this 
installation has solar assisted water heating system: 


(a) Industries which use hot water for processing; 

(b) All hospitals and nursing homes; 

(c) All hostels, hotels, motels, guest houses and banquet halls; 

(d) Large canteens i.e. which serve more than 100 persons in a day. 
(e) Office building on a plot area of 500 Square metres or above. 

(f) Residential buildings on a plot area of 500 Square metres or above. 
(g) Residential schools and colleges; 


Off Grid Roof Top Solar Power Plant at New Buildings: All buildings on 
plot size 300 Square metre or more, which are proposed to be constructed 
afresh, shall install Rooftop Solar Power installation, of adequate capacity, as

provisions of the Act, and other statutory rules under the Act. Wherever any 
discrepancy or ambiguity arises, the Act, shall apply and shall prevail. The provisions 
of the Act, 2006 are in-built into these Bye-Laws and shall be read as part of the Bye-

the said policy terms. To the said extent, the terms of these Building Bye-Laws are 
conditional.

99.0. 4706(E).— Whereas, section 10 (46A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961) provided for exemption 
of specified income of certain bodies or authorities or Boards or Trusts or Commissions, not being a company as may 
be notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette for the purposes of that section; 


And whereas, the Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961) was repealed by section 536(1) of the Income-tax Act, 
2025 (30 of 2025); 


And whereas, section 536(2)(a) and (b) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (30 of 2025), inter alia, provides that 
irrespective of the repeal of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961) (hereinafter referred to as the Act of 1961) and 
subject to sub-section (4) thereof, nothing shall affect- 


(i) | the previous operation of the provisions of the Act of 1961 and any order or anything duly done or 
suffered thereunder; or 


(ii) any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under the Act of 1961 or orders 
under that Act; 


And whereas, section 536(2)(c) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (30 of 2025) provides that the provisions of the 
Act of 1961 shall continue to apply to any proceeding pending on the date of commencement of the Income-tax Act, 
2025 (30 of 2025) and to any proceedings initiated on or after the 1* April, 2026 (including notices, assessment, 
reassessment, recomputation, rectification, penalty, reference, revision and appeals) in respect of any tax year beginning 
before the 17 April, 2026 and such proceedings shall be carried out as per the procedure specified in the Act of 1961; 


And whereas, section 536(2)(e) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (30 of 2025) provides that any proceeding pending 
on the date of its commencement before any income-tax authority or any other authority constituted under the repealed 
Income-tax Act, Appellate Tribunal, or any court, by way of application, appeal, reference or revision or by any other 
means, shall be continued and disposed of as if this Act had not been enacted; 


Now, therefore, in pursuance of the provisions of section 536(2)(a) to (c) and (e) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 
(30 of 2025), the Central Government hereby notifies, for the purposes of section 10 (46A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, 
"Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission” (PAN: AAAGMO0004R), a Commission constituted under the 
Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998 (No. 14 of 1998). 


This notification shall be effective for the assessment year 2026-27 relevant to the financial year 2025-26, 
subject to the condition that the assessee continues to be a Commission constituted under the Electricity Regulatory 
Commissions Act, 1998 (No. 14 of 1998) with one or more of the purposes specified in section 10 (46A) of the Income- 
tax Act, 1961. 


[Notification No. 116 /2026/F. No.195/13/2025-ITA-]]

The transporter will observe such restrictions as the State/Union Territory Government/National Highway

The transporter will obtain necessary prior permissions from the concerned departments of the State/Union 
Territory Government for the removal of any objects like hoardings, poles, signboards, transmission line 
shutdown etc. and observe such restrictions as the State/Union Territory Government/National Highway 
Authority of India/NHIDCL may by order specify in this behalf, before the vehicles are put on road. Cost of 
removal and redevelopment of any object permitted by the State/Union Territory Government shall be borne 
by the M/s Bhagyodaya Transport Limited. 


The transporter will give intimation at least ten days in advance and would need to obtain permission before 
commencement of transit, from concerned authority of State or Union Territory Authorities/National 
Highway Authority of India/NHIDCL en-route, in view of the oversized cargo. For each such movement, the 
timing should be prescribed by the concerned authority. 


If so directed by the Public works Department of a State/Union Territory/National Highway Authority of 
India/NHIDCL, the loaded vehicles will not be allowed to pass over or under the bridges on the roads in that 
State/Union Territory and in such cases applicants will have to make arrangements at their cost, after 
obtaining the permission from the concerned Authorities, to cross the rivers/drains. 


The transporter would be liable to pay such amount to the Government of State/Union Territory/National 
Highway Authority of India/NHIDCL or any other affected person where any damage is caused to the roads 
or road structures/bridges/other road users/persons directly or indirectly due to the movement of the trailers. 


Coupling of the trailers along the length of the road will be permissible only for above movements. 
The said vehicles should be moved without any hindrance to the normal flow of traffic. 


The vehicles should display all danger flags and lights, the vehicles should be preceded and followed by a 
vehicle displaying prominently that a heavy load is passing. 


The maximum speed of the trailers for movement on the road shall not exceed 5 km/hr. 


The trailers shall be painted for the entire width by yellow and black zebra stripes on the front and rear sides 
duly marked for night time driving/parking suitably by red lamps at the front and rear and red flags on both 
the sides during day time to indicate the extreme position of the vehicle clearly. 


The transporter will ensure that road taxes have been paid, fitness certificate, insurance cover(including Third 
Party Insurance), National Permit, and PUC have been obtained in respect of all the vehicles to be utilized 
during the above movement. 


No change will be made in the Registration Certificates of the Trailers and Prime Movers as they are already 
registered in the state of Nagaland, Maharashtra, Haryana, Gujarat and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman 
and Diu. 


In case of issues arising of any vehicle(s) or part of vehicle(s) out sourced from other registered owners, the 
transporter shall bear responsibility for the same. 


Any issue of any nature arising during the transportation of subject consignment shall be the responsibility of 
the transporter. 


The transporter must ensure that the installed VLT Devices (as per AIS-140) are activated during transit of 
the consignment. 


The transporter must ensure that the route does not have overhead structures, RoBs,RuBs, underpasses 
causing vertical constraint to the subject movement or the permission will be excluding the 
RUBs/FOBs/Overpasses for which the transporter shall make diversions for movement of ODC/OWC. 


The transporter must adhere to the guidelines by this Ministry vide letter RW/NH-35072/01/201 0- 
S&R(B)PT-2 dated 27th October, 2025.

an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections 
and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or

New Delhi, the 25th August, 2026 


S.O. 4747(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of NH 748A in the 
stretch of land from Km.136.100 to Km. 182.300 (NHAI BAGALKOT) in the district of BAGALKOT in the state of 
KARNATAKA, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section (1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Additional Deputy Commissioner 
(ADC in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity 
of being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making 
such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the 
objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Special District Revenue 
Officer,Land Acquisition, National Highways, Vellore in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent 
Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after 
hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, 
by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

Notice under Section 20A of the Railways Act-,1989 


S.O. 4722(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 20A of the Railways (Amendment) Act, 
1989 (24/89) (here in after referred as the said Act.), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for the public purpose, the 
Land, brief description of which is given in the schedule annexed here to, is required for the execution of the Special Railway Project, 
namely, “37१ & 47 Line from Jarapada to Sambalpur City (254.4 Km)” in the district of Anugola in the state of Odisha, hereby 
declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of the notification in 
the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section (1) of section 20D of 
the said Act. 


Every objection shall be made to the competent authority, namely Land Acquisition Zone Officer, Talcher-Sambalpur Rail 
Link Project, Anugola, State-Odisha for Construction of 3" & 47 Line from Jarapada to Sambalpur City (254.4 Km), in writing, and 
shall set out grounds thereof and competent authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or through 
a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further inquiry, if any, as the competent authority 
thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (2) of 20D of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected by the 
interested person at the aforesaid office of the competent authority.

परिसंघों को सहायता' (एएनएसएफ स्कीम) स्कीम को जारी रखने का अनुमोदन किया है। यह स्कीम अंतरराष्ट्रीय 
प्रतियोगिताओं में उत्कृष्टता प्राप्त करने के उद्देश्य से भारतीय खिलाड़ियों और टीमों की तैयारी, प्रशिक्षण तथा सहभागिता के 
लिए सहायता प्रदान करने की प्रमुख तंत्र के रूप में कार्य करेगी। 


2. एएनएसएफ एक केंद्रीय क्षेत्र की स्कीम है, जिसके अंतर्गत अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रतियोगिताओं में उत्कृष्टता प्राप्त करने के 
उद्देश्य से देशभर से चयनित खिलाड़ियों के प्रशिक्षण, तैयारी और सहभागिता के लिए सहायता प्रदान की जाती है। राष्ट्रीय 


खेल परिसंघों (एनएसएफ) से अपेक्षा की जाती है कि वे अपने कार्यकलापों के वित्तपोषण के लिए स्वयं के संसाधन जुटाएं तथा 
इस स्कीम के अंतर्गत उपलब्ध कराई जाने वाली वित्तीय सहायता अनुपूरक प्रकृति की होगी।

3. स्कीम के प्रमुख उद्देश्य निम्नलिखित हैं: 


Vi. 


Vii. 


Vil. 


भारत और विदेशों में आयोजित होने वाले ओलंपिक खेलों, पैरालंपिक खेलों, एशियाई खेलों और राष्ट्रमंडल 
खेलों सहित अंतरराष्ट्रीय खेल प्रतियोगिताओं में भारतीय खिलाड़ियों और टीमों की तैयारी, प्रशिक्षण तथा 
सहभागिता के लिए सहायता प्रदान करना। 


राष्ट्रीय खेल परिसंघों (एनएसएफ) के माध्यम से खिलाड़ियों को व्यापक सहायता उपलब्ध कराना सुनिश्चित 
करना, जिसमें प्रशिक्षण, प्रतियोगिता एक्सपोजर, खेल विज्ञान तथा अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर SHEA प्राप्त करने 
के लिए आवश्यक अन्य विशिष्ट सहायता शामिल है। 

राष्ट्रीय खेल परिसंघों (एनएसएफ) की व्यावसायिक दक्षता और वित्तीय प्रबंधन को सुदृढ़ करना तथा उपयुक्त 
जवाबदेही के साथ वित्तीय सहायता का सुव्यवस्थित, पारदर्शी और समयबद्ध प्रवाह सुनिश्चित करना। 

भारत में अंतरराष्ट्रीय खेल प्रतियोगिताओं की मेजबानी के लिए राष्ट्रीय खेल परिसंघों (एनएसएफ) को वित्तीय 
सहायता प्रदान करना, ताकि वैश्विक खेल प्रतियोगिताओं के आयोजन के लिए राष्ट्रीय क्षमता को सुदृढ़ किया 
जा सके। 

ओलंपिक खेलों, एशियाई खेलों और राष्ट्रमंडल खेलों सहित बड़े बहु-खेल आयोजनों, जब भी ऐसे आयोजनों का 
दायित्व देश को सौंपा जाए, की मेजबानी में सहायता करना | 


राष्ट्रीय खेलों और राष्ट्रीय चैंपियनशिपों के आयोजन में राज्यों, भारतीय ओलंपिक संघ (आईओए) और राष्ट्रीय 
खेल परिसंघों (एनएसएफ) को सहायता प्रदान करना, जो घरेलू प्रतियोगिता तथा प्रतिभा पहचान की रूपरेखा 
के प्रमुख घटक हैं। 

जमीनी स्तर पर खेलों के विकास और क्षमता निर्माण को बढ़ावा देना, जिसमें कोचों, तकनीकी अधिकारियों 
और सहायक कर्मियों का विकास शामिल है, ताकि विभिन्न खेल विधाओं में दीर्घकालिक आधार पर पर्याप्त 
प्रतिभा-संसाधन सुनिश्चित किया जा सके। 


देशज खेलों को बढ़ावा देना तथा उनके वैश्विक विस्तार के लिए राष्ट्रीय खेल परिसंघों (एनएसएफ) को वित्तीय 
सहायता प्रदान करना, जिसमें विश्वभर के अग्रणी विश्वविद्यालयों और खेल अकादमियों के साथ सहयोग 
शामिल है। 


अंतरराष्ट्रीय परिसंघों और विदेशों में समकक्ष राष्ट्रीय परिसंघों के साथ अपने संबंधों तथा प्रतिष्ठा को सुदृढ़ करने 
में राष्ट्रीय खेल परिसंघों (एनएसएफ) को सहायता प्रदान करना; अंतरराष्ट्रीय खिलाड़ियों को भारत में प्रशिक्षण 
के अवसर उपलब्ध कराना; तथा वैश्विक खेल समुदाय में भारत की सद्भावना और पहचान में वृद्धि करना।

खिलाड़ियों के लिए खेल किट हेतु सहायता; शिविर में भाग लेने वाले खिलाड़ियों के लिए चिकित्सा बीमा हेतु सहायता; 
विदेशी प्रशिक्षण/प्रतियोगिता एक्सपोजर हेतु हवाई यात्रा के लिए सहायता; विदेशों में आयोजित प्रतियोगिताओं के लिए 
रेफरी/जज/अंपायर/तकनीकी अधिकारियों की प्रतिनियुक्ति हेतु सहायता; विदेश में आवास एवं भोजन तथा जेब खर्च भत्ते के

सांस्कृतिक आदान-प्रदान और अंतरराष्ट्रीय सहयोग के लिए सहायता; प्रशासनिक जनशक्ति की नियुक्ति के लिए सहायता; 
चिकित्सा मूल्यांकन और खेल विज्ञान संबंधी प्रोटोकॉल के लिए सहायता; तथा विभाग में परियोजना प्रबंधन इकाइयों

MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
(Department of Sports) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 24th August, 2026 


SUBJECT: ASSISTANCE TO NATIONAL SPORTS FEDERATIONS SCHEME - REG. 


F. No. 12-11/2026-Gov-1.— The Government approved the continuation of the Scheme of ‘Assistance to 
National Sports Federations’ (ANSF Scheme) for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, as the principal mechanism for 
supporting the preparation, training and participation of Indian sportspersons and teams for achieving excellence in 
international competitions. 


2. ANSF is a Central Sector Scheme which provides assistance for training, preparation and participation of selected 
sportspersons, from across the country, for achieving excellence in international events. National Sports Federations 
(NSFs) are required to raise their own resources to finance their operations, and the financial support available under 
the Scheme is supplemental in nature. 


3. The major objectives of the Scheme are: 


i. 


ii. 


lil. 


iV. 


Vi. 


Vii. 


To support preparation, training and participation of Indian sportspersons and teams in international 
sporting events, in India and abroad, including the Olympic Games, Paralympic Games, Asian Games and 
Commonwealth Games. 


To ensure provision of comprehensive athlete support through NSFs, including training, competition 
exposure, sports science, and other specialised support required for achieving excellence at the 
international level. 


To strengthen professional competence and financial management of NSFs, and to ensure streamlined, 
transparent and timely flow of financial assistance with appropriate accountability. 


To provide financial assistance to NSFs for hosting international sporting events in India, so as to 
strengthen national capacity for conduct of global sports events. 


To support hosting of mega multi-sport events, including the Olympic Games, Asian Games and 
Commonwealth Games, as and when awarded to the country. 


To assist States, IOA and NSFs in conduct of National Games and National Championships, as core 
elements of the domestic competition and talent identification framework. 


To promote grassroots development and capacity building, including development of coaches, technical 
officials and support personnel, to ensure sustainable bench strength across sports disciplines.

collaborations with leading universities and sports academies worldwide. 


ix. 10 support NSFs in strengthening their relationships and standing with International Federations and 
counterpart national federations abroad; offering training opportunities to international athletes in India; 


and enhancing India’s goodwill and recognition within the global sporting community. 


4. Main components of the Scheme are: Assistance for conduct of National Championships both for Men and 
Women in Senior, Junior and Sub Junior age categories for meeting expenses towards Boarding & Lodging, Hiring of 
FOP/Equipment, Accessibility Audit, Accessible Transportation, Payment of Technical Officials and Prize Money; 
Assistance for National Games towards sports equipment, Timing, Scoring and Result (TSR) services, remuneration to 
Technical officials and technical conduct; Allocation of funds for grassroot development; Assistance for hosting of 
international tournaments in India for meeting expenses towards Boarding, lodging & transportation, Rent of playfields, 
Cost of consumable equipment, Certificates, medals and awards, Prize money, Payment of remuneration and travel to 
Technical Officials/Referees/ Umpire/Jury, Hosting / competition sanction fee, Uniform for technical officials/ referees/ 
Umpire/Jury, Dope testing and any other statutory expenses, Event insurance, Expense on electricity incurred during 
the conduct of the international event, Accessibility Audit and Accessible Transportation; Assistance for engagement 
of High Performance Directors, Foreign Coaches, Foreign Experts, National Chief Coach, other Coaches; Assistance to 
NSFs for engagement of support personnel such as sports medicine doctors, physiotherapists, Psychologist etc; 
Assistance for National Camps/Training in Academies; Training of the Elite athletes at the Olympic Training Centres; 
Assistance towards Travel from place of stay to national camp/foreign training/ competition & back; Assistance towards 
boarding & lodging etc. for national camps and non-camp days dietary allowance for focus group athletes; Assistance 
towards Field of play charges for camps / Championships; Assistance towards Sports kit for campers; Assistance 
towards Medical Insurance for campers; Assistance towards air travel for foreign training / competition exposures; 
Assistance towards deputation of referees/ judges/ umpires/Technical officials for competitions abroad; Assistance 
towards boarding & lodging abroad and payment of out of pocket allowances; Assistance towards Ceremonial Dress 
and Kit Charges for multi-sports events; Assistance towards transportation, hiring of equipment, infrastructure, 
consumables; Assistance towards training of Sports Scientists, coaches and support personnel; Expenditure on dope 
control; Purchase of equipment; Assistance for indigenous sports for global outreach; Assistance for Cultural Exchange 
and International Cooperation; Support for engagement of administrative manpower; Assistance towards Medical 
Assessment and sports science protocols; Engagement of Project Management Units (PMUs) in the Department for 
managing specific issues relating to planning, coordination with national and international stakeholders, having bearing 


on international standing of the country in the comity of sporting nations. 


5. Proposals of NSFs for training, coaching, participation in international events, hosting of international sports 
events, engagement of coaches and support personnel etc are considered in meetings of the Annual Calendar of Training 


and Competitions (ACTC), chaired by Secretary (Sports). 


6. The Department of Sports, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and the Sports Authority of India (SAT) shall 
be responsible for operationalising the Scheme and for its overall implementation and monitoring. Guidelines for 
implementation of the Scheme of Assistance to NSFs will be issued by the Ministry and communicated to NSFs and 
other concerned stakeholders.
